title: Intermittent composition across time is a strobed chain's composition, and in linear chains it is arrival
subject: When composition of two contacts across time, holding at some lags but not all, is fixed by the chain itself
conclusion: For a chain of three rings joined by two shared contacts, the lags at which the far contact binds the two end rings recur with the period P of the chain's T-step maps; the chain observed only at the lags of one residue modulo P composes at every observed lag or at none, so intermittent composition is persistent composition of a strobed chain whose phase is the only input the chain does not fix, an input the doctrine forbids an observer to supply unless the chain singles the phase out. For linear or affine rules with affine contact laws, the chain composes exactly at the lags where its far contact depends on both end rings, so the composing lags are the arrival lags of both ends' influence; in any chain, composition implies that dependence.
